page.title: Memory, capacity and performance
page.description: What a tinyactors actor costs in memory, how to size a host, how each operation's cost holds as the population doubles, and its conformance to SCXML.

hero.headline: Small actors, flat costs.
hero.lede: What an actor costs in memory, how to size a host, and how each operation's cost holds as the population doubles. Every number comes from a program in the repository that you can run.

section.heading: What an actor costs.
section.p: One more actor, message or delayed send, measured as resident memory in a process with a million of them.

table.caption: Measured 2026-11-20 on an Intel Xeon at 2.10 GHz, 4 CPUs, 16 GiB, Linux; Node.js 22.23.5 and Bun 1.4.1. A counter chart with one variable, messages of {"text": "hello"}, tracing on.

section.p: A host's fixed costs spread over its actors, so an actor costs less in a larger population.

section.heading: Size a host.
section.p: A host grows on its own, but each growth copies its memory. A host that will hold a known population is better sized for it.
Read what a host uses at any time:

section.heading: Costs stay flat.
section.p: Every operation of the API, timed on a host of two million actors and on one of four million. Each cell is the cost at two million, then at four, and their ratio. A test fails when a ratio passes 1.5.

table.section: Work does not grow with the population
table.caption: Most actors hibernated in SQLite, at most 1000 resident. Measured 2026-10-17 on an Intel Xeon at 2.10 GHz, 4 CPUs, 16 GiB, Linux; Node.js 22.23.3 and Bun 1.4.1. Microseconds.

section.heading: Correct by the standard.
section.p: The core passes all 191 automatic tests of the W3C's SCXML test suite. Every binding runs the same conformance suite, on each of its datamodels.
